items.title: Wayne Andre interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 7, 2002
items.q: I took Leon Cox’s place as a matter of fact... when he left — I never did play first trombone in that band

ctx.x: Oh yeah. Bands in those days were playing public dances, which you don’t see anymore, in a ballroom in Indiana or something like that, that all the bands went through, Lake Compounce, Connecticut, all the bands went through, and you’d play at officers clubs, NCO clubs in the service, and the big thing too bands did in those days, yeah, I remember that in this band, is you’d go into a college and you would play a dance on Friday night, a concert on Saturday afternoon and a dance Saturday night. So that was like a…

so when I moved up from third trombone to second trombone, when he left — I never did play first trombone in that band — I learned a lot from Vinnie Forchetti, who was playing first trombone in that band for the last part of the time I was on it. I learned a lot from him. But I had one guy in back of me who loved me dearly, he was kind of a jokester, his name was Buddy Hanna and everything else, and he played kind of like Sweets Edison you know and stuff like that. But he’d yell down at me and says, “Stop playing…
